questions.heading: Every Rule Is One Linear Row, and a Ratio Is Multiplied Out Before It Is Written
questions.stem: A rule says the training budget t must be at least 15% of the total spend t + e + m, where e and m are the two other budgets. Which row states the rule in a form MathOpt accepts?

options.says: The share is of the whole total, t included; leaving t out changes the rule.
MathOpt refuses a division by an expression with variables (TypeError).
Multiplying out puts the total on the side of 0.15, not t.
Right: multiply both sides by the total, which is never negative, so the direction stays.

questions.heading: GLOP Solves It: Read the Status, Then the Amounts, Then the Rows
questions.stem: A program-split LP returns OPTIMAL with $150k of a $2,000k budget unspent. Two programs sit at their crew limits, and the third sits exactly at its share cap. The CFO asks why the money was left. Which answer is right?

options.text: GLOP stopped early, and a better split would spend the full $2,000k
options.says: OPTIMAL means the split is proven best; no allowed split is worth more.

options.text: The plan is right, since that money has nowhere useful left to go
options.says: Right: the money has nowhere allowed to go, so the budget row has room.

options.text: The budget row should be an equation, so GLOP would then spend it all
options.says: An equation would force spending that no rule allows: the model would be infeasible.

options.text: Moving the $150k to the cheapest program would raise the value further
options.says: Every program is stopped by a full row; none can absorb more.

questions.heading: A Changed Number Moves the Answer Only Through the Rows That Are Full
questions.stem: In a program-split LP, the budget row has $300k of room and the vegetation crew row is full. One director offers $200k more budget; another offers one more vegetation crew-month. Which offer can raise the value?

options.text: Only the crew-month, because extra money would sit unused
options.says: Right: loosening a row with room changes nothing; a full row is what holds the answer.

options.text: Only the budget, because crew rows carry no dollar value
options.says: Crews limit spend through their row; a full row is exactly what holds the answer.

options.text: Both offers, because either one loosens a row of the model
options.says: A row with room is not holding the answer, so more of it changes nothing.

options.text: Neither offer, because the split is already OPTIMAL as it stands
options.says: OPTIMAL is best for the current numbers; changing a full row's number moves the answer.
